title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Payment Methods and Changes of Method
content:
The claimant of an Unemployment Benefit Claims record chooses how benefits are paid:

- direct deposit to a checking or savings account in the claimant's name;
- the state benefit debit card, which is assigned by default when no direct deposit election is made; or
- a paper check where neither is possible.

## Terms of a change

1. Retired clause, no longer in force: "A change takes effect for payments issued on or after the payment method effective date, which is the change lead time after the change is recorded, counted in business days (Monday through Friday excluding state holidays)." This clause is superseded by the current basis.
2. A payment method change is accepted only while the claim hold reason is not fraud review. A claim whose hold reason is none, nonmonetary issue or identity verification accepts the change.
3. Only the claimant may ask for the change, and a request from anyone else is not accepted.
4. One replacement debit card per benefit year carries no fee; later replacements carry the card program's fee and do not change the payment method.

## Points of judgement

| Hold reason on the claim | Change of method |
|---|---|
| None | Accepted |
| Nonmonetary issue | Accepted |
| Identity verification | Accepted |
| Fraud review | Not accepted |

A second replacement debit card in the same benefit year carries the card program's fee, and the claimant's payment method remains the debit card.
